title: On top of spaghetti…. …or all by themselves: babies love meatballs! 🍝...
description: On top of spaghetti…. …or all by themselves: babies love meatballs! 🍝🎉 ✔️Ground beef may be introduced as soon as baby is ready to start solids, which is generally around 6 months of age. ✔️Cooked ground beef is a protein-rich food that is often high in fats to fuel baby’s rapid growth. It is also filled with other essential nutrients, such as iron, zinc, selenium, choline, and vitamin B6 which developing babies need.  ✔️Meat is a common choking hazard, though ground beef is less of a risk than, say, a cube or chunk of steak, which doesn’t fall apart as easily. By age:  ➡️ 6mos+ : Mix ground beef that has been cooked well-done into an easy-to-scoop food like mashed potatoes, polenta, or mashed veggies. Alternatively, prepare burgers, meatballs, or patties that are at least 2 inches (5 cm) in diameter and cooked until the internal temperature reaches 160 F (71 C). Make sure the cooked burger or meatball is soft enough to be easily smushed by baby’s gums.  ➡️ 9 mos+: Break meatballs or burger patties into small, bite-sized pieces to offer an opportunity for babies and toddlers to practice their pincer grasp and fine motor skills. If baby is not quite ready to pick up smaller pieces of food, you can continue to offer ground beef in sauces or as whole burgers, kebobs, meatballs, or patties that are at least 2 inches (5 cm) in diameter and cooked until the internal temperature has reached 160 F (71 C). Dipping the meat in applesauce, guacamole, yogurt, or other sauces can aid swallowing. ➡️ 18 mos+ : This age can be a good time to serve a whole hamburger (as a sandwich with a bun and other toppings, rather than deconstructed with the bun and patty consumed separately). Continue to cook the meat until it has reached an internal temperature of 160 F (71 C).  ⭐️ For complete details on how to serve any food to babies, including ground beef, download the Solid Starts  App at the link in our bio  #babyledweaning #firstfoods #solidstarts #100firstfoods #blwtips

title: When first starting solids, a “meal” is often just 1 or 2 pieces of f...
description: When first starting solids, a “meal” is often just 1 or 2 pieces of food. There’s no need to offer a full plate with multiple options, as many babies may find this overwhelming. Instead, focus on one or two options prepared in an age-appropriate way.  Keep in mind that a baby who is just learning to taste, explore, and chew solid foods will not actually consume much at first as they’re building up their self-feeding skills.  As baby grows, you can gradually increase their options, while still serving each food in an age-appropriate way.  What about portion sizes? Follow baby’s lead, there’s no need to control baby’s portion sizes or food intake. Baby will let you know if they’re full by losing interest in the meal, turning their head away, or throwing their food. If baby is interested in having more, they may grunt, reach for more food, or vocalize or signal for more food. Remember: Common allergens should be introduced separately from other new foods and tracked closely. You can do this in our app.  ➡️ For details on how to prepare any food according to baby’s age, download the Solid Starts app 📱 #SolidStarts #startingsolids #solidfood #5monthsoldbaby #6months

With:  ✔️ Color  ✔️ Texture  ✔️ Flavor  ✔️ Variety  The reason so many toddlers prefer bland foods is because many parents assume that’s all they can have when they start solids (think: rice cereal & oatmeal), so of course babies develop a preference for bland foods.  But you can actually begin introducing flavor, texture, and different ingredients (even spice!) as soon as your baby is ready to start solids. This is typically around 6 months.  ⚠️ Remember: Egg is one of THE most common food allergens and should be introduced separately from other foods so you can rule out potential allergies. title: 🚨 Wait! Before your baby takes their first bite, make sure they are a...
description: 🚨 Wait! Before your baby takes their first bite, make sure they are actually ready.  Starting solids isn’t about hitting a certain age — it’s about hitting these 4 developmental milestones first: ✅ Sits independently with minimal support ✅ Can hold their head up  ✅ Reaches, grabs, & brings toys to their mouth (without toppling over!) ✅ Shows interest in your food — leaning in, watching intently, mouthing things Most babies get there around 6 months, but every baby’s timeline is different — and that’s okay. Some babies show signs of readiness a little bit earlier while some babies need a bit more time. The safest way to begin is to wait until your baby reaches each of the above milestones. So if your 6-month-old isn’t quite there yet, it’s always worth waiting another week or two. Focus on bringing them to the table to watch you eat and give them plenty of time to move freely on the floor. #startingsolids #babyledweaning #solidstarts #signsofreadiness #blwtips

title: Your baby doesn’t need a single tooth to start solid foods. And we’re...
description: Your baby doesn’t need a single tooth to start solid foods. And we’re not talking about purées either. 😳 It’s one of the biggest myths about starting solids and we get it — it seems totally counterintuitive. But your baby chews with their strong gums—not their teeth. In fact, the molars we use for chewing don’t typically arrive until after the first birthday. That means waiting for teeth could delay valuable opportunities to practice chewing skills and explore new foods when your baby is developmentally ready.  Instead of looking for teeth, look for signs of readiness: ✔️good head control ✔️the ability to sit with minimal support ✔️bringing objects to their mouth while seated  ✔️an interest in food Once those signs are all there, your baby can begin their solid food journey—teeth or no teeth. 🥑🥦🍓  ➡️ Wondering which foods your baby can begin with? title: Citrus Safety🍊 Whole citrus segments still in the membrane (and espec...
description: Citrus Safety🍊 Whole citrus segments still in the membrane (and especially small varieties of citrus like mandarin oranges, tangerines and clementines) pose a choking risk because of their tapered shape and because the membrane is challenging to pierce. One way to reduce choking risk is to “supreme” the fruit, or remove each citrus segment from its membrane.  Another way is to offer large orange wedges on the rind, a particularly good option if baby doesn’t have teeth yet. With large orange segments, baby is forced to suck on it, rather than putting the whole thing in their mouth. Baby biting off pieces of the rind? Take a breath and let them work it out, and consider moving to supreming. ➡️ Start your free seven day trial of the Solid Starts app at the link in our bio ✔️ #babyledweaning #firstfoods #blwtips

title: In the event of a severe allergic reaction, always administer epineph...
description: In the event of a severe allergic reaction, always administer epinephrine first, then call for emergency medical help.  Once you’re ready, follow these steps:  1️⃣ Locate your child’s epinephrine injector or EpiPen and remove it from its case 2️⃣ Place your thumb on the inside with your fingers wrapped around it and remove the blue top 3️⃣ Holding your child as still as possible on your lap, or having someone else hold the child, locate the largest muscle of baby’s mid-thigh with your hand 4️⃣ Place the orange end of the epinephrine pen over baby’s thigh and press down. It’s ok to administer through clothing 5️⃣ Hold for 3 seconds then release If you’re using an Auvi-Q auto-injector, you’ll notice that it contains a small speaker which plays step-by-step instructions. To administer the epinephrine from the Auvi-Q:  1️⃣ First remove it from the case 2️⃣ Remove the red bottom 3️⃣ Place that end over the largest muscle of baby’s mid thigh. It’s ok to administer through clothing.  4️⃣ Press down until you hear a “click and hiss” 5️⃣ Hold for two seconds and then release EpiPen instructions apply to Mylan/Viatris manufactured generics as well. Other devices may have slightly different instructions. Always review the use instructions on your own device and practice with a trainer device if available. Following the administration of epinephrine from any device, you should still seek emergency medical help for your child. Follow the guidance on your child’s written emergency action plan. If you cannot reach your doctor, call emergency services or head to your nearest emergency room for further evaluation.  ⚠️ If your child’s symptoms are not improving within 3-5 minutes of the 1st dose of epinephrine, administer a second epinephrine autoinjector to the other thigh and call for emergency medical assistance. If emergency help is on the way, stay on the line with the operator and follow instructions. Questions? 🤍

title: Babies love sardines! 🐟 (really!) Sardines are among our top 10 choic...
description: Babies love sardines! 🐟 (really!) Sardines are among our top 10 choices of fish for babies. ⚠️ Finned fish like sardines are a common food allergen. Unfortunately, most individuals who are allergic to finned fish do not outgrow the allergy. About 40 percent of people with finned fish allergies don’t experience their first allergic reaction until adulthood. By age: ➡️ 6 mos+: Offer whole fresh sardine fillets, cooked and with bones removed, or whole sardines from a can. Canned or packaged sardines can be offered with skin and bones intact, as both are made soft and edible by the canning process. Serve on its own as finger food or mashed and mixed with soft foods like cooked vegetables or grains for baby to scoop. ➡️ 9 mos+: As baby develops the pincer grasp (where the thumb and forefinger meet), try offering a sardine fillet broken into flakes for the child to try to pick up. You can also continue to offer big pieces or the whole fillet. ➡️ 12 mos+: Continue to offer flakes of sardine fillet, either as finger food or for utensil practice. You can also mix the flakes into cooked grains, pastas, or vegetables  📲Start a free trial of the Solid Starts app at the link in bio  #babyledweaning #blw #blwtips

title: Deep breaths….we can explain 🙃 Pizza is a polarizing topic whenever w...
description: Deep breaths….we can explain 🙃 Pizza is a polarizing topic whenever we discuss it. But here’s the thing: many families enjoy it all over the world and it’s easy to make at home using ingredients your family loves. Afterall it’s just dough, tomatoes, cheese and anything else you choose to include!  Additionally, pizza crusts are resistive in nature making them an excellent food teether to offer baby to help build important oral motor skills. And while pizza crust isn’t necessarily unbreakable, it does soften as baby munches, which has many benefits as well.  Food teethers stimulate two key chewing reflexes: the tongue lateralization reflex and the phasic bite reflex. Practicing with a food teether encourages baby to repeatedly use these movements, which builds muscle memory for chewing. Food teethers are also easy for babies to hold and move in, out, and around their mouths while activating senses with flavor. This helps babies build a “mental map” of their mouths, which they need for thorough chewing. So…will you be giving your baby a pizza crust? 🍕 #babyfood #babyrecipes #6monthsold

title: Wait to wipe 🧽 While some babies don’t mind at all, the vast majority...
description: Wait to wipe 🧽 While some babies don’t mind at all, the vast majority of babies will react negatively to frequent and/or aggressive wiping of their face and hands during and after mealtime.  To help baby avoid negative associations with their high chair, try these tips for cleaning up:  1️⃣ Prepare baby. Try not to surprise or catch them off guard with wiping 2️⃣ Bring a pitcher of water to the table to help with cleanup or if you can, move directly to the sink 3️⃣ Use soft wipes for baby’s face which can be extra sensitive especially after consuming acidic foods  4️⃣ Sing a favorite song or play music to lighten the mood 5️⃣ Count it Out. Give baby a set time for how long cleanup will last  And if all else fails, guide their hand with a washcloth to show them how it’s done or hand it over to give them a bit of ownership in the process.  More clean up tips? Drop them in the comments.  #SolidStarts  #babyledweaning #babyledweaningideas #firstfoods #whatmybabyeats

title: Want a low-risk, high-reward food? Hand over a mango pit! 🥭 Our feedi...
description: Want a low-risk, high-reward food? Hand over a mango pit! 🥭 Our feeding therapists LOVE mango pits for babies starting solids. Here’s why:  ✔️Baby gets challenge without the risk. ✔️Mango pits are large and firm, making them easy for babies to pick up. (Rolling in almond flour or even rice cereal will aid grip.) ✔️Mango pits give baby an opportunity to work oral reflexes that are foundational to chewing. When baby munches on a mango pit, it works a tongue reflex responsible for moving food to the side of the mouth, as well as muscles necessary for biting and chewing. We caregivers often put nutrition first when we think about food for our babies. But selecting foods that will work baby’s oral-motor skills is equally important ➡️ For details on how to introduce any food to baby, download the Solid Starts App at the link in our bio.  #SolidStarts #FingerFoodFirst #babyledweaning #babyledfeeding #babyled

title: ⭐️ Want to see these demos for every food? You can find them in the S...
description: ⭐️ Want to see these demos for every food? You can find them in the Solid Starts App 📲 Now where were we?  Hot dogs are a major choking risk. 🌭⚠️ The good news? You don’t have to serve them to your child if you don’t want to. Our goal is to help those who do want to serve them know how to do it in a way that minimizes risk.  🫶 Additionally, a food like hotdog may be what is accessible to many families. We’re here to serve everyone. If you choose to serve them, here is how our feeding experts suggest minimizing risk:  ➡️ 6 mos +: Try to avoid, since hot dogs pose a high risk of choking. If you do decide to offer a taste of hot dog at this age, make sure it is cooked thoroughly, remove the casing if there is one, finely chop the meat, and stir the pieces into a soft, scoopable food. ➡️ 12 mos +: Cut cooked hot dog into quarters lengthwise, creating long, thin sticks that the toddler can practice biting. When serving, be sure the child is seated and that a caregiver is an arm’s length away. When offering hot dog at this age, avoid cutting it into rounds, half-moons, or small quarters. These shapes can actually increase the risk of choking. Serving long strips of hot dog encourages the child to take bites of the food, increasing the likelihood of chewing and priming the brain to further break down the food. ➡️ 18 mos +: Cut cooked hot dog lengthwise into long halves, or continue cutting into long, quartered sticks. When serving, be sure the child is seated and that a caregiver is an arm’s length away. When offering hot dog at this age, avoid cutting it into round sections or bite-sized pieces. These shapes can actually increase the risk of choking. ➡️ 24 mos +: At this age, toddlers may be ready to practice eating a whole hot dog (with the bun, as desired) once they are demonstrating mature eating skills #SolidStarts #babyledweaning #babyledweaningideas #firstfoods #whatmybabyeats

title: It’s called “baby led” for a reason 🤏 At around six months old, your ...
description: It’s called “baby led” for a reason 🤏 At around six months old, your baby has all the foundational skills they need to learn how to safely eat solid food.  Let’s break it down:  When you serve your baby a bigger piece of finger food, they have all the fine motor, gross motor, and cognitive skills they need to reach out, pick up that food, and bring it to their mouth — which naturally teaches them how to chew it.  We’re not rushing them through their development. We’re meeting them right where they’re at developmentally. This helps them build important new skills.  That said, when we serve a baby a puree and we spoon feed them, we are encouraging them to take in larger and larger amounts of that puree because it is a pretty easy thing for a baby to do. So really quickly, we move them towards full meals of purees, which replaces the breast and the bottle feeds that should be foundational before 12 months of age.  So rather than us meeting baby where they’re at, we’re actually moving them towards eating larger amounts before they need to.  Baby-led weaning on the other hand is meeting baby right where they’re at developmentally and giving them tons of time to explore and slowly build the skills they need before we ever think about them taking in a full meal.  So the next time someone tells you not to “rush” your baby into solid foods, you can remind them that: You’re not rushing your baby. You’re not trying to fill their belly. You’re helping them build new skills.  You’re following their lead. 🤍

title: At 9 months, it’s time to go…smaller 🫐 Here’s why:  Around nine month...
description: At 9 months, it’s time to go…smaller 🫐 Here’s why:  Around nine months, most babies start using their fingers to form what’s known as a “pincer grasp” to pick up and move small objects. 👌 A pincer grasp simply means the tips of the thumb and index finger come together, a motion we use to pick up small items, pull zippers, and button shirts. Before babies develop a pincer grasp, they will use their whole hand-their fingers and palm together-to pick up, hold, and bring food into their mouths.  This is why, prior to 9 months, we serve large pieces of food. It’s the only size a baby can pick up and bring to their own mouth before the pincer grasp develops.  Why does that matter?  The research tells us that the act of self feeding is protective against choking, and in order for a baby to self feed, they must be able to pick up the food on their own. Prior to nine months they don’t yet have the motor skill to do that with small pieces.  This is a big change that happens, but keep in mind. some babies may develop their pincer grasp sooner than 9 months and others may need a little bit more time. Questions?  ➡️ There are some things you can do to help your baby refine their pincer grasp. Search “pincer grasp” in our app to read more. You can download it at the link in our bio. 🎉

title: Are food tethers safe? Yes, food teethers are safe for babies as soon...
description: Are food tethers safe? Yes, food teethers are safe for babies as soon as they are ready to start solids, which is generally around 6 months of age. ➡️ Because they are long, hard sticks of food that will not break as baby munches, food teethers cannot be shoved in the mouth all at once. ➡️ Food teethers are also easier for baby to move in, around, and out of the mouth than purees and mashes, which can spread on the tongue and lead to more gagging. ➡️ Because food tethers are also unbreakable, baby can practice the motions of chewing without needing to move food toward the back of the mouth to swallow. ➡️ As pediatric feeding and swallowing specialists, we have worked with thousands of babies-including hospitalized babies with medically complex needs- -and we know that there are tremendous benefits that help baby learn to chew in a low-risk way. description: Mess now → confidence later! 🧽✔️ When your baby squishes, smears, and plays with food, their brain is learning before they ever take a bite. title: Sleepy baby? 🥱 Save this post. Feeding a tired baby might seem harmle...
description: Sleepy baby? 🥱 Save this post. Feeding a tired baby might seem harmless, but it can increase the risk of choking — this is because proper posture is necessary for safe swallowing.  When babies are overtired, their coordination, alertness, and swallowing reflexes aren’t at their best. They’re more likely to slump, lean back, or lose the upright position needed for a safe swallow. This makes it harder to control food and protect their airway. ✔️Baby should be upright, with feet well-supported, and alert  ✔️Head, neck, and trunk aligned (not slouched or tilted back in the high chair)  Baby too tired to participate in the meal? Skip it entirely or end it early if you notice these signs during the meal and offer a breast or bottle feeding instead.  Is this an ongoing issue?  This is common at dinner. Consider bumping up dinner time by an hour if possible or if baby is under a year skip dinner and offer a breast or bottle instead.  ➡️Check out mealtime schedules page in the Solid Starts App for more ideas. Link in bio.

title: Raw apple is risky for babies & toddlers 🍎 Raw apple and dried apple ...
description: Raw apple is risky for babies & toddlers 🍎 Raw apple and dried apple pieces are common choking hazards. But let’s be real for a moment:  If baby bites off a piece of any food, their chewing reflexes kick in and they will continue to try to chew that food and mash it with their gums. But because raw apple pieces are hard to breakdown, baby is more likely to attempt to swallow them whole — so we recommend avoiding this risk. How?  Cook apple until soft for babies 6 months+ or slice your apple thinly at 9 months+. While apple skin can cause gagging and lots of spitting, the skin itself does not pose much choking risk. ⭐️ Download the Solid Starts App at the link in bio for complete details by age.

title: When your baby is gagging the last thing you want to do is stand up. ...
description: When your baby is gagging the last thing you want to do is stand up. 🪑 While our automatic reaction to seeing our kids struggle, may be to stand up out of surprise, this is not an ideal reaction when your baby gags. When you stand up, your baby tends to look up at you, which puts gravity working against them.  When a baby’s head is looking up and their neck is extended, gravity is pushing the food backwards, which is the exact opposite of what we want to do during a gag. Instead: kneel down next to your baby so they look down at you or at least keep their head from extending too far backwards as this helps the gag reflex move the food forward and out of the mouth. 🤍

title: Go fish! 🐟 Sardines are among our favorite first fish for babies. Pac...
description: Go fish! 🐟 Sardines are among our favorite first fish for babies. Packed with omega-3 fatty acids, sardines are also rich in protein for energy and growth and vitamin B12 for healthy blood and brain development, as well as many more essential nutrients for growing babies.  Sardines are also one of the few naturally-occurring food sources of vitamin D and among the fish lowest in mercury in all of the sea. Here’s how to serve:  ➡️ 6 mos+: Offer whole fresh sardine fillets, cooked and with bones removed, or whole sardines from a can. Canned or packaged sardines can be offered with skin and bones intact, as both are made soft and edible by the canning process. Serve on its own as finger food or mashed and mixed with soft foods like cooked vegetables or grains for baby to scoop. ➡️ 9 mos+: As baby develops the pincer grasp (where the thumb and forefinger meet), try offering a sardine fillet broken into flakes for the child to try to pick up. You can also continue to offer big pieces or the whole fillet. ➡️ 12 mos+: Continue to offer flakes of sardine fillet, either as finger food or for utensil practice. You can also mix the flakes into cooked grains, pastas, or vegetables ⭐️Tap the link in bio to learn more! #pescatarian #babyfood #firstfoodsforbabies #blw #solids
